cards.name: Alpha Levels
cards.summary: Legacy Levels for the alpha channel only, on a 0-255 scale (probably the 8-bit version): remaps transparency with input/output black and white points and gamma. It tightens or softens a keyed or masked edge; on fully opaque footage only Output White Level changes anything (it fades the whole layer). Listed in the hidden '_Obsolete' category (kept so old projects open), not in the normal Effects menu.
use_for: crushing the semi-transparent fringe left by a green-screen key of a presenter
hardening a soft feathered mask edge on a cut-out leader photo
uniformly fading a layer through Output White Level in old project files
avoid: new work: use Levels (Individual Controls) alpha controls, Simple Choker or Matte Choker
does nothing visible on an opaque press photo or video unless Output White Level is lowered
Output Black Level above 0 makes fully transparent areas partly opaque: a dark box appears around a cut-out
values are 0-255 here; do not reuse numbers from the 0-1 version (ADBE Alpha Levels3)

params.name: Input Black Level
params.does: alpha at or below this becomes fully transparent (removes faint fringe)

params.name: Input White Level
params.does: alpha at or above this becomes fully opaque (solidifies a soft edge)

params.name: Gamma
params.does: bends the mid-transparency values; below 1 thins the edge, above 1 thickens it

params.name: Output Black Level
params.does: minimum alpha of the result; above 0 the transparent surround of a cut-out becomes visible

params.name: Output White Level
params.does: maximum alpha of the result, i.e. overall opacity

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Levels (Individual Controls) (ADBE Pro Levels2) Alpha controls, or Simple Choker / Matte Choker for edges; Premiere: no alpha-levels effect (Alpha Adjust only scales opacity; Ultra Key Matte Cleanup chokes/softens a keyed edge)
cards.scripting: Obsolete twin of ADBE Alpha Levels3: all level values are 0-255, Gamma 0-10. Five plain 1d sliders, no dropdowns. Works on alpha only, so on an opaque layer only Output White Level is visible (demo: 128 = half opacity, the frame darkens over the black comp background). For new builds use ADBE Pro Levels2 ('Alpha Input Black' etc., 0-1 scale).

verified.note: Whole frame drops to about half brightness (half opacity over the black comp background), exactly the Output White Level 128 fade the card describes.

It tightens or softens keyed or masked edges; on opaque footage only Output White Level has an effect. Listed in the hidden '_Obsolete' category (kept so old projects open), not in the normal Effects menu.
use_for: removing a faint halo around a keyed presenter
firming up a feathered cut-out of a politician or object
fading a whole layer in old templates through Output White Level
avoid: new work: use Levels (Individual Controls) alpha controls, Simple Choker or Matte Choker
values are 0-1 fractions here; 0-255 numbers from the 8-bit version get clamped to 1
no visible change on an opaque frame unless Output White Level is lowered
Output Black Level above 0 makes fully transparent areas partly opaque (dark box around a cut-out)

params.name: Input Black Level
params.does: alpha at or below this becomes fully transparent

params.name: Input White Level
params.does: alpha at or above this becomes fully opaque

params.name: Gamma
params.does: bends mid-transparency; below 1 thins the edge, above 1 thickens it

params.name: Output Black Level
params.does: minimum alpha of the result; above 0 the transparent surround of a cut-out becomes visible

params.name: Output White Level
params.does: maximum alpha (overall opacity)

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Levels (Individual Controls) (ADBE Pro Levels2) Alpha controls, or Simple Choker / Matte Choker for edges; Premiere: no alpha-levels effect (Alpha Adjust only scales opacity; Ultra Key Matte Cleanup chokes/softens a keyed edge)
cards.scripting: Same property names as ADBE Alpha Levels2 but every level is a 0-1 fraction (Gamma 0-10). Plain 1d sliders, no dropdowns. Alpha only: on opaque footage only Output White Level shows (demo 0.5 = half opacity). Prefer ADBE Pro Levels2 alpha controls for new builds.

verified.note: Byte-identical to the 0-255 version at 128: Output White Level 0.5 fades the whole frame to half opacity over black.

cards.name: Apply Color LUT
cards.summary: Legacy version of Apply Color LUT: grades the layer through a LUT file (.cube, .3dl and similar) chosen in a file dialog when the effect is applied in the UI. With no LUT loaded it leaves the image unchanged. Listed in the hidden '_Obsolete' category (kept so old projects open), not in the normal Effects menu.
use_for: keeping old projects that convert log camera footage to Rec.709 rendering the same
re-rendering an old template that carries a channel's signature film-look LUT
avoid: new work: use Apply Color LUT (ADBE Apply Color LUT2) or Lumetri Color's Input LUT / Look
a script cannot set the LUT file: the only harvested entries are headers ('<LUT not set>')
applying it can open a file dialog that stalls an unattended run
cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Apply Color LUT (ADBE Apply Color LUT2); Premiere: Lumetri Color (Basic Correction Input LUT, Creative Look)
cards.scripting: No settable properties: both harvested entries are headers ('<LUT not set>'). The LUT is chosen in a file dialog at apply time; pve/dialog_watchdog.py exists to cancel the LUT-file dialog that 'Apply Color LUT' opens during a scripted harvest, so run it alongside any unattended build that adds this effect. With the dialog cancelled or absent no LUT is loaded: verified 2026-10-04, all 10 frames of the gallery render are byte-identical to the untouched AE render (identity). For scripted LUT grades use ADBE Apply Color LUT2 via a hand-saved .ffx preset with the LUT loaded (layer.applyPreset) or Lumetri Color; see their cards.

verified.note: Frame is byte-identical to the untouched AE render: with no scriptable LUT property the effect is an identity pass; needs a hand-made .ffx preset with a LUT loaded to demonstrate.
verified.second_opinion: corrected: scripting said both 'may block on the dialog (unverified which)' and 'did not block the run'; the batch finishing does not prove no dialog (pve/dialog_watchdog.py exists to cancel this effect's LUT dialog and gallery.py does not record whether it ran), so the text now keeps the dialog warning and states only the verified identity result. Agree with verdict broken and needs_input (10/10 frames byte-identical to the untouched render, md5 820db19...).

cards.name: Box Blur
cards.summary: Legacy box blur: averages neighbouring pixels in a square. More Iterations make it smooth and close to a Gaussian blur; 1 iteration gives a blocky, boxy blur. Same controls, ranges and dropdown as the current Fast Box Blur. Listed in the hidden '_Obsolete' category (kept so old projects open), not in the normal Effects menu.
use_for: blurred background plate behind a quote card or lower third
blur-in / blur-out reveal at the start or end of a shot
horizontal-only blur for a quick speed-streak whip feel
avoid: new work: use Fast Box Blur (ADBE Box Blur2) or Gaussian Blur
Iterations 1 at a large radius looks blocky and cheap
with Repeat Edge Pixels off the frame edges go soft and transparent (dark border on a full-frame shot)

params.name: Blur Radius
params.does: blur size in pixels
params.typical: 10-40 for background plates, 60-150 for a heavy blur

params.name: Iterations
params.does: number of box passes; more = smoother, Gaussian-like

params.name: Blur Dimensions
params.does: direction of the blur (dropdown)
params.typical: 1 both, 2 horizontal for a speed streak

params.name: Repeat Edge Pixels
params.does: checkbox: keep the frame edges solid instead of fading to transparent

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Fast Box Blur (ADBE Box Blur2); Premiere: Fast Blur / Gaussian Blur
cards.scripting: Same property names, ranges and dropdown order as ADBE Box Blur2, so a spec can swap the match name unchanged. Blur Dimensions is 1-based: 1 Horizontal and Vertical, 2 Horizontal, 3 Vertical. Repeat Edge Pixels is a 0/1 checkbox.

verified.note: The whole photo is evenly and heavily blurred (faces, stripes and foreground blocks lose all detail) with solid frame edges, as described for radius 30, 3 iterations.

cards.name: Brightness & Contrast
cards.summary: Legacy brightness and contrast: shifts every tone up or down and stretches or flattens the tonal range. The old maths clips highlights and shadows quickly at large values (same behaviour as 'Use Legacy' in the current effect). Listed in the hidden '_Obsolete' category (kept so old projects open), not in the normal Effects menu.
use_for: quick lift of a dark archival or phone clip
bright flash on a beat by keyframing Brightness up and back
keeping old templates that already use it rendering identically
avoid: new work: use Brightness & Contrast (ADBE Brightness & Contrast 2) or Lumetri Color
large values clip faces, flags and white shirts to flat white or black

params.name: Brightness
params.does: adds or removes overall brightness
params.typical: -25 to 25 for correction; 60-100 for a flash (may not reach pure white; use Exposure for a white-out)

params.name: Contrast
params.does: stretches (positive) or flattens (negative) the tonal range
params.typical: 10-30 for punch, -20 for a faded look

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Brightness & Contrast (ADBE Brightness & Contrast 2; its 'Use Legacy (supports HDR)' checkbox gives the old behaviour); Premiere: Brightness & Contrast
cards.scripting: Two 1d sliders, both -100 to 100 (the current effect allows Brightness -150 to 150). No dropdowns. Legacy maths; use the current match name 'ADBE Brightness & Contrast 2' for new builds.

verified.note: Frame is clearly brighter with stronger contrast; the white wall and white clothing clip toward flat white, as the card warns.

cards.name: CC Composite (obsolete)
cards.summary: Legacy CC Composite: blends the layer's original, un-effected image back with the result of the effects above it in the effect stack, using a blend mode and opacity. The current CC Composite (CS Composite) can also take another layer as Top Layer. Listed in the hidden '_Obsolete' category (kept so old projects open), not in the normal Effects menu.
use_for: laying the sharp original back over a blurred copy for a soft-glow dream look in a flashback
restoring natural colour over a heavy stylised effect stack at partial opacity
avoid: first or alone in the stack it composites the image with itself, so little or nothing changes
new work: use CC Composite (CS Composite) or an effect's own blend-with-original control

params.name: Opacity
params.does: strength of the original composited back on

params.name: Composite Original
params.does: blend mode used to lay the original over the effected result (dropdown, 41 entries)

params.name: RGB Only
params.does: checkbox: composite colour channels only and keep the effected alpha

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: CC Composite (CS Composite); Premiere: none (stack a duplicate clip with a blend mode)
cards.scripting: Must sit AFTER (below) the effects whose result it blends with; alone it is a near no-op, so demo_settings are left empty and the gallery frame is expected unchanged. Composite Original is a 1-based blend-mode dropdown with 41 entries counting separators: 1 Copy, 2 Behind, 3 In front (default), 5 Darken, 6 Multiply ... 13 Screen ... 18 Overlay ... 41 Luminescent Premul (enum_labels (read from After Effects 26.0)). RGB Only is a 0/1 checkbox. Prefer the current match name 'CS Composite' for new builds. Verified 2026-10-04: alone with defaults the gallery frame is byte-identical to the untouched AE render, confirming the no-op. A demo needs a stacked render (e.g. Fast Box Blur above it, CC Composite below at Opacity 50) that the single-effect gallery does not do.

verified.note: Frame is byte-identical to the untouched AE render: alone in the stack it composites the image over itself; needs a stacked demo with an effect above it.
verified.second_opinion: agree: all 10 rendered frames are byte-identical to the untouched AE render (same md5 as Separate XYZ Position / Set Matte defaults); at the default Composite Original mode it is identity alone, so a stacked demo is needed and needs_input is right.

cards.name: CC PS Classic (obsolete)
cards.summary: Legacy CC Particle Systems: replaces the layer's image with animated particles on black that burst out, fade from a birth colour to a death colour and fall or drift with gravity and turbulence (the default Animation draws four-point star sparkles). Superseded by CC Particle Systems II. Listed in the hidden '_Obsolete' category (kept so old projects open), not in the normal Effects menu.
use_for: spark or confetti burst behind a title reveal
rising embers on a trailer title card
keeping an old template's particle look
avoid: new work: use CC Particle Systems II or CC Particle World
the default yellow-to-green colours look dated; always set Birth/Death Color
no emitter position in the harvest, so placement cannot be scripted
replaces the layer's own image with particles on black: apply it to a separate solid and composite with Add or Screen
high Birth Rate with long Longevity piles the sparkles into a blown-out white frame

params.name: Birth Rate
params.does: how many particles are emitted
params.typical: 5-20 (with Longevity 1; 50 with Longevity 2 blew the frame out)

params.name: Longevity (sec)
params.does: how long each particle lives

params.name: Velocity
params.does: launch speed of the particles

params.name: Gravity
params.does: downward pull; negative values make particles rise

params.name: Turbulence
params.does: random wobble of the particle paths

params.name: Max Opacity
params.does: peak opacity of the particles

params.name: Birth Color
params.does: colour at emission

params.name: Death Color
params.does: colour at end of life

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: CC Particle Systems II (CC Particle Systems II) or CC Particle World; Premiere: none
cards.scripting: Animation is a 1-based dropdown (read from After Effects 26.0): 1 Explosive, 2 Sideways, 3 Fire, 4 Bonfire, 5 Twirl, 6 Fountain, 7 Viscouse, 8 Scatterize, 9 Sparkle, 10 Vortexy, 11 a separator, 12 Rain Drops, 13 Star Light (default), 14 Smokish, 15 Bubbly, 16 Bally, 17 Watery Drops, 18 Experimental. Colours are "#RRGGBB". There is no emitter/Producer position property in this classic version (low certainty where it emits; likely layer centre). Render confirmed the source image is replaced: particles draw on black, so put it on its own solid layer. Birth Rate 50 with Longevity 2 blew about 80% of the frame out to white; keep Birth Rate x Longevity well under that (Birth Rate 10 with Longevity 1 rendered as separate, readable sparkles spread over the whole frame). The simulation runs from the layer's start time, not its in-point: in the gallery the trimmed clip starts 1.5 s before the comp, so the very first comp frame was already full of particles. Use CC Particle Systems II for new builds.

verified.note: With Birth Rate 10 / Longevity 1 and the warm colours, the frame now shows separate gold four-point star sparkles fading to deep red on black across the whole frame, where the old render was about 80% blown out to white (the photo is still replaced, as the card already warns).

Superseded by CC Particle Systems II. Listed in the hidden '_Obsolete' category (kept so old projects open), not in the normal Effects menu.
use_for: sparks spraying from a point behind a logo or title
falling embers across the top of a trailer card
keeping an old template's particle look
avoid: new work: use CC Particle Systems II or CC Particle World
default yellow-to-red colours look dated; set Birth/Death Color
replaces the layer's own image with particles on black: apply it to a separate solid and composite with Add or Screen

params.name: X Radius

params.name: Y Radius
params.does: vertical size of the emitter area

params.name: Birth Rate

params.name: Longevity (sec)

params.name: Death Color

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: CC Particle Systems II (CC Particle Systems II) or CC Particle World; Premiere: none

Opacity is 0-1, not 0-100

festive or nostalgic mood on a title card
avoid: new work: CC Snowfall (CSSnowfall) has depth and looks more natural
snow over a sunny summer press shot looks fake
Opacity is 0-1, not 0-100

cards.name: CC Time Blend
cards.summary: Accumulates frames over time so anything moving leaves smeared, fading trails (an accumulating echo). The Transfer mode and Accumulation decide how bright and how long the trails are. Listed in the hidden '_Obsolete' category (kept so old projects open), not in the normal Effects menu.
use_for: light-trail smear on night traffic or rally-crowd B-roll
dreamy flashback ghosting in a documentary
streaky hit on a fast reel cut
avoid: still photos or locked-off shots with nothing moving show no change at all
the result depends on rendering frames in order from the layer start; partial renders or scrubbing can differ
new work: Echo or CC Wide Time are deterministic per frame

scripted aerender gave erratic output, not trails: in a 10-frame render of moving footage from the comp start, 8 frames were near-black faint ghosts (about 6-12% of normal brightness) and 2 frames were a full-brightness copy of a later source frame with white speckles

params.name: Transfer
params.does: blend mode used to accumulate frames (dropdown, 18 entries)

params.name: Accumulation
params.does: how much of the previous build-up is kept each frame = trail length

params.name: Clear To
params.does: what the accumulation buffer resets to (2-entry dropdown)

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Echo (ADBE Echo) or CC Wide Time; Premiere: Echo
cards.scripting: Transfer is a 1-based dropdown: 1 Blend (default), 2 Composite Over, 3 Composite Under, 4 Screen, 5 Add, 6 Soft Light, 7 Hard Light, 8 Lighten, 9 Darken, 10 Multiply, 11 Difference, 12 Color, 13 Overlay, 14 Luminosity, 15 a separator, 16-18 the Classic Blend / Composite Over / Composite Under. Clear To: 1 Transparent (default), 2 Current Frame. Both read from After Effects 26.0. Accumulation is 0-1. Stateful: each frame depends on the previous ones, so render from the layer's first frame; aerender of a sub-range may not match a full render. Needs motion in the clip to show anything. Verified 2026-10-04: the gallery rendered the whole 0.4 s comp (10 frames in order from the comp start, moving footage with exposure flashes) and grabbed frame 5; it was not a single-frame render. Frames 0-6 and 9 were near-black faint ghosts, frames 7 and 8 both showed source frame 8 at full brightness; no trails anywhere. Possible causes (untested): the trimmed clip's layer start is 1.5 s before the comp start so the buffer never saw the layer's first frame, or AE renders frames out of order (Multi-Frame Rendering) so the state is not carried. A demo needs a clip whose layer start equals the comp start and a full-length sequential render; do not rely on it in automated builds, use Echo instead.

verified.note: All 10 rendered frames show no trails: frame 5 (the gallery frame) is almost black (about 7% of the untouched brightness) with a faint ghost, and frames 7-8 jump to a full-brightness copy of a later source frame. This was a 10-frame sequential aerender of moving footage, so the accumulation does not work in the scripted render path as built.
verified.second_opinion: corrected: the first rewrite blamed a 'single-frame / aerender of one frame' render and asked for 'a sequence render of moving footage', but gallery.py renders the whole 0.4 s comp (10 frames, 25 fps) of moving footage and grabs 0.2 s; the full render (renders/G242.mp4) is erratic, not trail-free-black throughout. Fixed the avoid entry, scripting and note, lowered confidence to low. Agree with verdict broken and needs_input.

cards.name: CC Time Blend FX
cards.summary: Two-instance version of CC Time Blend: the Instance popup marks a start copy and an end copy, so only the effects placed between the two copies get accumulated into smeared motion trails. Listed in the hidden '_Obsolete' category (kept so old projects open), not in the normal Effects menu.
use_for: accumulating only a glow or colour effect into trails while the base image stays clean
keeping old templates that use the sandwich setup rendering the same
avoid: a single instance does little: it needs a matching start and end copy
stateful accumulation: partial renders or scrubbing can differ from a full render
new work: Echo or CC Wide Time are simpler and deterministic

params.name: Instance
params.does: marks this copy as the start or end of the sandwich (2-entry dropdown)
params.typical: 1 Copy on the upper instance, 2 Paste on the lower one

params.name: Transfer
params.does: blend mode for the accumulation (dropdown, 18 entries)
params.typical: 1 Blend (default); the same 18-entry list as CC Time Blend

params.name: Accumulation
params.does: trail length (share of previous build-up kept)

params.name: Clear To
params.does: what the buffer resets to (2-entry dropdown)

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Echo (ADBE Echo) or CC Wide Time; Premiere: Echo
cards.scripting: Needs TWO instances on the same layer: one with Instance = 1 above the effects to smear and one with Instance = 2 below them (Instance (read from After Effects 26.0): 1 Copy, 2 Paste; the pairing is untested). A single instance (as in the gallery) is expected to show little or no change, so demo_settings are empty. Transfer: 1-based, 18 entries. Clear To: 1-based, 2 entries. Accumulation 0-1. Stateful: render from the layer start. Needs motion in the clip. Verified 2026-10-04: the single-instance gallery frame is byte-identical to the untouched AE render. A demo needs two instances (start and end) around another effect, rendered as a sequence of moving footage; note that single CC Time Blend gave erratic, trail-free output in the same 10-frame gallery aerender, so a sandwich demo may fail the same way.

verified.note: Frame is byte-identical to the untouched AE render: one instance alone does nothing; needs the two-instance sandwich and a sequence render of moving footage.
verified.second_opinion: agree: all 10 rendered frames are byte-identical to the untouched AE render, so one instance alone is identity and needs_input is right; added a pointer that CC Time Blend's own sequential render was erratic, so the two-instance demo is not guaranteed to work either.
